en: Preface to the Publication of the *Commentary on the Meaning of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra* I once saw in the *General Catalogue of the Teachings* (*Jiaozang Zonglu*) by the Celestial Head of the Sangha (Tiansengtong) that: "The *Commentary on the Meaning of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra* in four fascicles was composed by Huiyuan.
Consequently, I remarked that my own ancestor, the Great Master Zhiyi, had frequently cited this work when composing his commentary on the *Amitābha Sūtra*.
Adopting Jingying’s [commentary] for the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* would likewise be appropriate.
Recently, a bookseller brought a volume of the *Yiji* (Commentary on the Meaning) to me; I received it with great joy.
Upon reading it, although it does not quite match my original expectations, its explanations are most thorough.

When he elaborates on a single point, he frequently first raises the preliminary inquiry and only then provides the resolution; this truly preserves the structural integrity of the fundamental matrix (*mātṛkā*), such that even Jiaxiang of Guanzhong could not rival him.

My ancestor, Master Shi, was perfectly accomplished in both principle and phenomena; yet he took contemplation of principle as his primary focus, while his explanations of phenomena were somewhat brief. Therefore, would it not be appropriate to first read this record and subsequently integrate it with the harmonious discourse of Master Zhi?
However, there are many errors and omissions; may those who later obtain a good edition take the trouble to correct them.
Written on the first day of the tenth month of winter in the Renchen year of the Zhengde era, by the śramaṇa Kātō of Hōshu at Enryaku-ji. Preface respectfully composed.
